chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Saif ibn 'Amirah from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and a man asked him about a man who fell ill and made a vow to God in gratitude that if God healed him, he would give charity from his wealth in a large amount, but did not specify an amount. So what do you say?

He said: 'He should give charity with eighty dirhams, for that will suffice him, and that is clear in the Book of God when He says to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): "God has certainly helped you in many places." And 'many' in the Book of God is eighty.'
ai.seo_question: What is the sufficient amount for an unspecified vow of charity in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Shia juristic principle of interpreting 'many' (kathir) as a specific numerical value, here set at eighty dirhams, to resolve ambiguity in unspecified vows of gratitude (nadh al-shukr). The Imam grounds this legal deduction in the Quranic phrase 'in many places' (8:7), establishing a precedent where linguistic quantification informs fiqh. This reflects the scholarly tradition of deriving precise legal obligations from general Quranic terminology to ensure clarity in religious practice.
